name: Katahdin via the Knife Edge
why: Up Maine's highest mountain and across the Knife Edge, a granite arête a metre wide between Pamola Peak and Baxter Peak, the end of the Appalachian Trail.
book: Katahdin Trailhead Pass (parking reservation) for Roaring Brook, on the Baxter State Park reservations site; gate closes when lots are full. Trails open only in the summer season and close in bad weather: check the park's trail status.
water: Water at Roaring Brook and Chimney Pond (treat it); none above treeline.
dangers: The Knife Edge is exposed with drops of 600 m on both sides: never in wind, rain or fog.
There is no easy way off the Knife Edge once you are on it.
Long day: rangers advise turning back by noon.
turnaround: Be on Pamola Peak by 11:00 in good weather, or come down via the Saddle Trail from Chimney Pond.

points.name: Roaring Brook Campground
points.note: The trailhead on the east side of the mountain.

points.name: Pamola Peak
points.note: The end of the Helon Taylor ridge and the start of the Knife Edge.

points.name: Baxter Peak

points.name: Chimney Pond
points.note: A pond in the great basin under the cliffs, with a ranger station.
